name: body-explorer
description: The Living Body Atlas & Health Intelligence Platform: Interactive 2D/3D anatomy, evidence-graded food spectrum, regulatory safety registry, and emergency triage protocols.
conventions: Mandatory Plain Language: From now onwards, all added content, tips, UI text, and explanations must use simple, everyday words that are easy to understand for everyone (Grade 6-8 reading level, zero unexplained jargon)
All components use named exports, never default exports
Strict TypeScript typing - zero use of 'any'
Hindi translations paused: all newly added content and UI copy must remain English-only until explicit resumption is requested by user

Individual food intelligence only: Whole-Body Food Atlas (15 organs), Unusual Food Science (6 mechanisms), and Interactive Food Journey grounded in ICMR-NIN 2024 standards. Keep live shuffling active across all sections.
architecture_patterns: SSR via TanStack Start and Nitro Vercel preset
Local-first state with Zustand and localStorage persist

file_structure.src/components: UI components, interactive anatomy, and feature views
file_structure.src/data: Evidence-based health datasets, nutritional hierarchies, and registries

patterns: Unit tests for all utility functions
Component tests for interactive UI elements

sprint_focus: Building the user onboarding flow with email verification and profile setup.
never_do: Never use dense medical jargon, biochemical terms, or complicated words without immediate simple everyday explanations — all words must be easy to understand
Never add Hindi translations (hi: ...) to content, tips, or UI text — Hindi translation is strictly paused until the user explicitly asks to resume
Never add meal prep, recipes, or meal plans to the nutrition hub — strictly provide individual food nutrient intelligence, biological roles, and clinical limitations
Never use useEffect for data fetching — use Server Components or SWR
Never store secrets in .env files committed to git
Never use inline styles — always use Tailwind classes
Never use `any` TypeScript type — always type explicitly
Never mix database queries into React components
Never output verbose unsolicited recaps, exhaustive changelogs, or repetitive summaries that waste tokens — mention ONLY the most critical points unless explicitly asked
Never use purple gradients, pill buttons, fake reviews/metrics/counters, vague hero text, emoji icons, em dashes, crazy scroll/cursor animations, or AI slop photos/copy on websites
Never let an AI grade its own work without independent gate verification
Never leave completed work uncommitted or unpushed to GitHub
Never run unsolicited background daemons, update pollers, or indexing services on Arch Linux
preferred_patterns: Always use simple, easy-to-understand words for all content and UI copy ('Kitchen Table Test') so anyone can understand without a medical background
Practice extreme token economy: keep responses concise, high-signal, and directly answer user requests without unprompted changelogs or filler
Use Zod for all schema validation
Use Drizzle ORM for all database access
Use Next.js Image component for all images
Always mandate production web essentials: custom domain, custom favicon suite, remove AI badges, /privacy page, and /terms page
Always follow the 6-step Second Brain closed loop: Load Conventions -> Select Model -> Autonomous Loop -> Validate Output -> Continuous Learning -> Automated Git Push
Always enforce Arch Linux On-Demand System Governance (run interactive tools on-demand, terminate completely on exit)
